newsitem.title: SWEDEN: New CEO seen as boost to Electrolux - analysts.
newsitem.headline: New CEO seen as boost to Electrolux - analysts.

text.p: The change of guard at Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB signals a new era with incoming chief executive Michael Treschow known as a cost-cutter with a focus on shareholder value, analysts said on Tuesday.
Treschow, currently chief executive of industrial engineer Atlas Copco, takes over at Electrolux from Leif Johansson who is moving to vehicle maker Volvo AB to succeed retiring Soren Gyll.
Markets reacted positively to the news and Electrolux shares closed 12 up at 438 on Monday. The share was three higher at 441 crowns at 1400 GMT on Tuesday.
Analysts said Treschow's aggressive reputation and his ability to implement change justified the gains.
"We see clear indications that Treschow at Atlas Copco has been very focused on improving shareholder value," Kleinwort Benson analyst Peter Lawrence told Reuters.
He said the hope was that Treschow's performance would be repeated at Electrolux where the balance sheet was weaker than at Atlas Copco with net debt to equity ratio close to 100 percent.
Electrolux, the world's leading supplier of household appliances, last Friday disappointed the market by posting lower-than-expected earnings for 1996.

The company reported a 19 percent drop in profits after financial items to 3.25 billion crowns ($446 million) with sales slipping five percent to 110 billion crowns. Electrolux, echoing U.S. rival Whirlpool, blamed a weaker European market.
"So we're looking for him to be rigorous about cost cutting and strengthening the balance sheet," he said.

Nordbanken analyst Paul Hansson said Treschow had successfully cut costs at Atlas Copco where he worked for 22 years. This included six years as chief executive when he gave shareholders an average 13 percent annual rise in dividends.

"Electrolux is basically a cost-cutting case because there are very small possibilities of increasing prices," Hansson told Reuters. "It's such a mature market that everthing needs to be done on the cost side.
"He is considered a strong and competent managing director and has an excellent track record from Atlas Copco."
While Electrolux's share price gained on the new appointment, Volvo shares barely moved, which some analysts interpreted as a vote of poor confidence in Johansson.

"One of the criticisms of Electrolux is that they've been slow...in implementing strict cost control or fully utilising the potential of the acquisition strategy that they had in the 1980s," said one Stockholm-based analyst.
"The cost-cutting potential increases enormously with Treschow -- which is why I think it is positive for Electrolux."
Analysts also said bringing new blood into the company indicated faster changes could be expected.
"This is the first externally-recruited CEO since 1967. I think it is so that he has completely different potential for cutting costs," an analyst said.
Unibank analyst Henrik Breum said Treschow was known for being aggressive and had a skill for integrating companies.
"I think the changes that have taken place at Atlas Copco...show he's capable of taking drastic measures," he said.
"Treschow has shown he's good at integrating different companies because Atlas has bought a lot of companies."
($1=7.29 crowns)
